To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in Argentina and Brazil the regulation of work has been influenced by the organization of the production process, which has been strongly internationalized.

the regulation of work is a complex phenomenon that is not only influenced by the organization of the production process, but also by other sources of regulations that are configured in different ways in each place.

the labour law in both countries has been unable to regulate the employment relationship in the advertising film industry, which has resulted in the prevalence of informal employment and the absence of social rights for workers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of work, understood as the set of legal and extra-legal rules, which determine the conditions of the employment relationship.
two main questions. First, how is the regulation of labour in this sector in Argentina and in Brazil? And second, what are the similarities and differences of this regulation in the two countries?

the following questions: What are the similarities and differences between the regulation of work and the forms of organization of the work process in the advertising film industry in Argentina and Brazil, in a context of strong internationalization of outsourcing and the consequent instability of the employment relationship? What are the similarities or differences in the role of labour legislation and trade unions in the two countries? How do these differences and similarities influence the forms of organization and regulation of the work process?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the labour legislation and trade unions in both countries are unable to effectively protect the rights of workers in the advertising film industry.

in both cases the labour legislation was not able to prevent the deterioration of labour conditions, and that in the Brazilian case, trade union action was not able to stop the advance of the most precarious forms of work.

the labour legislation has been the main source of regulation in both cases, and that the trade unions have been the main actors of regulation in the Brazilian case, and the main source of conflict in the Argentinian case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in spite of the similarities, in Argentina and Brazil the regulation of work and employment in the film sector is marked by the coexistence of different sources of regulation that are configured according to the specificities of each country and the particularities of the sector.
the regulation of the work in this sector has a dual nature, in that it is both uniform and diverse.

, in both Argentina and Brazil, the regulation of work was strongly influenced by the productive process, which was characterized by the internationalization of production chains, outsourcing and the use of precarious forms of work.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in both countries there has been a convergence between the regulation of work, which is based on a labour law model of protection of the worker, and the forms of organization of production that are based on the outsourcing of work and the precariousness of the workforce.
, in spite of the fact that both countries have a similar legal and regulatory framework, the effects of this framework are different.
the regulation of work is not only the result of a set of legal rules and labour relations, but also of the way in which the productive process is organized.
